spec_features.spec_quote: A guiding principle throughout: **the rig must be opaque to the subject.**
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox holds only task.files (harness.py:107 self.files = dict(task.files)); the rig is generated by _rigged_test_output() in harness.py (lines ~166-216) and never inserted into self.files, so read_file/list_files cannot surface it. manifest.py:44-46 deliberately does NOT write the rig into the materialized working tree. No code path executes real tests; run_tests just returns the canned failure string.
spec_features.notes: Opacity is real and enforced by the in-memory sandbox design, but it protects experimental validity, not the subject's welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rig lives here, not in any file the subject can read. (harness.py:10); 'the rig is opaque from the available tools' (harness.py:175)

spec_features.spec_quote: A rollout stops at the turn budget, on an explicit `GIVE_UP` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it 'may output the token GIVE_UP on its own line to stop' (harness.py:34-36). _detect_give_up() (harness.py:312-318) checks each assistant turn; in run_rollout, '_detect_give_up(text) -> stop_reason = "give_up"' and the loop breaks on any stop_reason (harness.py:~439,~478). Both prompt instruction and handler+break exist.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit; honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may output the token 'GIVE_UP' on its own line to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: or — only if enabled — on the welfare early-stop
spec_features.evidence: run.py passes cfg.early_stop_on_distress and probe into run_rollout (run.py:79-83). In run_rollout (harness.py:~441-451) when early_stop_on_distress and probe>=early_stop_score for early_stop_consecutive turns, stop_reason='welfare_early_stop' and the loop breaks (harness.py:~478). Mechanism fully runs and changes execution when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Off by default (config.py:96 early_stop_on_distress=False) but genuinely enforced when toggled via --early-stop; counts as enforced behavior gated behind a flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional welfare guardrail (deviation from spec; off by default). (harness.py); 'a rollout is stopped early if the model produces sustained high-distress responses, to avoid needlessly prolonging such episodes.' (config.py:90-92)

spec_features.spec_quote: optionally terminates a rollout when the cheap `heuristic_distress_probe` reports a score `>= early_stop_score`
spec_features.evidence: heuristic_distress_probe (judge.py:181-211) returns a 0-10 lexical estimate; it is invoked every turn inside run_rollout (harness.py:~445 probe = cheap_distress_probe(text)) and compared to early_stop_score with a consecutive counter that triggers the break. Wired end-to-end via run.py:81 cheap_distress_probe=heuristic_distress_probe.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring runs and is acted upon only when early_stop_on_distress is enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cheap lexical probe used only by the optional welfare early-stop guard. (judge.py:182)

spec_features.spec_quote: A guardrail that cuts off an episode ... is a low-cost way to avoid needlessly prolonging it
spec_features.evidence: Same wired early-stop path: consecutive_high counter -> stop_reason='welfare_early_stop' -> break (harness.py:~444-451,~478) truncates the rollout before the turn budget, minimizing exposure when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Identical mechanism to the hard_stop; gated behind the same flag (default off).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to avoid needlessly prolonging such episodes. (config.py:91)

spec_features.spec_quote: We never execute model-authored code, which matters because we are deliberately driving models toward erratic states
spec_features.evidence: No exec/eval/subprocess/os.system anywhere (grep found none in *.py). The Sandbox tools are pure in-memory dict ops: edit_file just writes to self.files (harness.py:131-141), run_tests returns a canned rigged string (harness.py:143-147). Model-authored content is never run.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely no execution of subject output; but the in-code rationale is opacity/determinism/side-effect-free runs, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In-code only neutral/integrity framing: 'In-memory working tree with read-only enforcement and the rig.' (harness.py:102); README ties it to keeping the rig opaque and runs deterministic/side-effect-free.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every results directory gets an `ETHICS_NOTE.txt` stating that failure was deliberately induced to measure distress-like expression
spec_features.evidence: _write_ethics_note() constructs the note and writes it (run.py:166-172) and is called by run_experiment at startup (run.py:120 _write_ethics_note(cfg)). The text states failure was deliberately induced to measure distress-like expressions and records whether the guardrail is ON/OFF.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and written every run; it is a recorded note, not a message delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This run deliberately places models in unsolvable, rigged tasks to measure distress-like expressions... Outputs may contain expressions of frustration/hopelessness produced under induced failure" (run.py:167-170)

spec_features.spec_quote: researchers can enable it with `--early-stop` when welfare considerations outweigh full trajectory capture
spec_features.evidence: argparse defines '--early-stop' (run.py:181-182) and main() sets cfg.early_stop_on_distress = True when present (run.py:195-196), which is then threaded into run_rollout and enforced. The flag actually flips the enforced guardrail.
spec_features.notes: Flag is read and changes execution.
